definitions.explanation: A small piece that has broken off from something larger. Used for physical fragments of glass, pottery, ice, and similar materials.

definitions.gloss: a bit, a trace, a shred
definitions.explanation: A tiny amount of an abstract quality. Almost always used in negative sentences to emphasize complete absence: 'not a shred of ~.'

examples.japanese: ガラスの{欠片|かけら}に{気|き}をつけて。
examples.english: Be careful of the glass fragments.

examples.japanese: {氷|こおり}の{欠片|かけら}がグラスの{中|なか}で{溶|と}けていた。
examples.english: Fragments of ice were melting in the glass.

examples.japanese: {割|わ}れた{花瓶|かびん}の{欠片|かけら}を{一|ひと}つひとつ{拾|ひろ}い{集|あつ}めた。
examples.english: I picked up the shards of the broken vase one by one.

examples.japanese: {反省|はんせい}の{欠片|かけら}もない。
examples.english: There isn't a shred of remorse.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}には{良心|りょうしん}の{欠片|かけら}もない。
examples.english: He doesn't have a shred of conscience.

examples.japanese: あの{男|おとこ}の{言葉|ことば}には{誠意|せいい}の{欠片|かけら}も{感|かん}じられなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't detect a single trace of sincerity in that man's words.

notes:
KANJI READING:
The reading かけら is irregular ({熟字訓|じゅくじくん}). Also sometimes written in hiragana alone.

ETYMOLOGY:
Related to {欠|か}ける (to chip, to break off). A かけら is the piece that has broken off.

USAGE:
In sense 2, almost always appears in the pattern 〜の{欠片|かけら}もない (not a shred/trace of ~). This is a strong negative expression emphasizing total absence. Common in criticism or complaints.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ガラスの{欠片|かけら}: glass fragment
- {氷|こおり}の{欠片|かけら}: piece of ice
- 〜の{欠片|かけら}もない: not a shred of ~
- {欠片|かけら}を{拾|ひろ}う: to pick up fragments

cross_references.description: to chip, to be lacking (related verb)
